newsitem.title: USA: British Air unveils 3-year, $10 billion makeover.
newsitem.headline: British Air unveils 3-year, $10 billion makeover.

text.p: British Airways Plc on Tuesday unveiled a three-year, $10 billion makeover that involves a new corporate identity and new services, products, aircraft, facilities and expanded employee training.

The airline, at a news conference in New York, said it will add 43 new aircraft to its fleet over the period: 29 Boeing 747-400s, nine 777s and five 757s. It also intends to spend hundreds of millions of dollars developing new routes, new services and products, and a new approach to customer service.
Other highlights of the plan include:
-- more partnerships along the lines of British Air's developing venture with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, with the goal of expanding service to more destinations worldwide;
-- $100 million in improvements to the airline's terminal at New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport, including improved road access;
-- a refurbishment of the check-in area at London's Heathrow Airport;
-- expanded departure options from the United Kingdom, including the development of London's Gatwick Airport as a second hub.
British Airways's American Depositary Shares fell 75 cents to $119.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
